AI consulting pricing: compare two pilot quotes

Two consultancies quote the same invoice-matching pilot. One includes a connector and training. The other expects your engineer to build the connector. Put the numbers on the same six-month timeline before discussing the day rate.

From quote to acceptance

Compare two published consulting scopes

A finance team deciding which invoices to automate needs different evidence from a team ready to test a matching application. These two UK G-Cloud 14 listings show what to ask for at each stage.

Digital Space · readiness assessment

Digital Space describes workshops, questionnaires and data exploration with IT and business teams. The work identifies use cases, assesses data quality and can outline a statement of work for a proof of value.

Published rate £595 to £1,495 per unit per day. Read Digital Space’s scope and pricing.

Suggested acceptance test Ask the finance lead to review the proposed use case, sample-data gaps and pilot plan. Can they decide whether to fund a build?

EY · application development

EY describes discovery, prototyping and application development through alpha and beta. Ask the bidder which phase the proposed fee covers and what software you receive at the end of it.

Published rate £200 to £2,600 per unit per day. Read EY’s scope and pricing.

Suggested acceptance test for a prototype Give the team held-back invoices. Have a clerk replay them and record matches, incorrect matches and referrals before signing off.

Record the quote you would approve

Ask each bidder to define a unit, list units by role and phase, and quote a capped fee. Add your team’s hours and usage charges. The published ranges alone cannot tell you which engagement will cost less.

Enter the bidders’ answers below. Print or save as PDF before closing the tab.

Agree on what the pilot must deliver

Write down the workflow start, the last permitted action and who accepts the result. For an invoice pilot, that might mean matching an invoice to an order, showing the discrepancy and sending it to a clerk. A quote that stops at extracting line items buys a different deliverable. Ask the bidder to mark every dependency as included, client-supplied or optional.

Count the hours your team supplies

In this illustration, the first quote includes integration for $15,000 and charges $450 a month for support. The second is $11,000 plus $750 a month and requires 40 hours from your engineer. At an illustrative loaded rate of $80 an hour, the second quote uses $3,200 of internal time. Replace these inputs with your own rates and the number of paid support months.

Price the decision after acceptance

Ask for the cost of keeping the pilot running for one additional month, exporting the data, and handing the integration to another operator. Check whether support starts at signing or at acceptance. A fee that starts during a delayed integration changes the total even if nobody changes the stated day rate.

Illustrative buyer scenario

A lower quote can use more of your team’s time

A finance manager receives two bids for invoice matching. One includes preparation of historical records. The other assumes her team will label every example. Before taking either bid to the CFO, she gives both bidders the same redacted batch and asks them to mark the work they expect her team to do.

Ask each bidder to price a second run after the buyer changes one matching rule. Require a separate figure for supplier work, clerk time and retesting. Keep the source invoices and answer key under the buyer’s control.

What to keep

A line-item quote, an owner for every input, and an acceptance sheet that both sides can run against held-back examples.

When to pause

If a bid promises accuracy without specifying how unresolved invoices count, return the bid for clarification before comparing prices.

Make the decision

Ask both bidders to sign off on the assumptions in the table. If one cannot price an unknown data-cleaning task, give it a capped discovery budget and a deliverable: a sampled error rate, a revised estimate and a decision date.
